name: Rowing machine
summary: Full-body cardio on an indoor rower. About 60 percent of the power comes from the legs, so the order of the stroke matters more than arm strength.
setup: Strap your feet so the strap crosses the widest part of your foot.
Set the damper to 3 to 5. A higher setting feels heavier but is not a harder workout; it mostly tires you sooner.
Hold the handle with a relaxed overhand grip, thumbs underneath, wrists flat.

steps.text: Start at the front: shins vertical, arms straight, body leaning slightly forward from the hips, like 1 o'clock on a clock face.
Push with your legs first. Arms stay straight and your back keeps its forward angle until your legs are almost flat.
Swing your body back from the hips to about 11 o'clock.
Finish by pulling the handle to your lower ribs, elbows passing close to your sides.
Go back in reverse order: arms away, body forward, then bend the knees and slide forward slowly. The return takes about twice as long as the drive.

jointCues.cue: Legs, body, arms on the drive. Arms, body, legs on the way back.
jointCues.why: The legs are the biggest engine. Pulling with the arms early wastes their power.

jointCues.cue: Low and relaxed through the whole stroke. Do not shrug at the finish.
jointCues.why: Shrugging tires the neck and upper traps and adds nothing to the stroke.

jointCues.cue: Draw them straight back past your ribs, close to your body, not winged out.
jointCues.why: This uses the lats and keeps the wrists flat.

jointCues.cue: Long and braced; the body hinges at the hips, not by rounding the lower back.
jointCues.why: Rounding under load at the catch strains the lower back.

jointCues.cue: Vertical at the catch, not past vertical.
jointCues.why: Coming too far forward puts the knees and hips in a weak, cramped position.

breathing: Breathe out during the drive, breathe in during the recovery. At higher stroke rates take an extra quick breath at the finish.
tempo: Easy rowing: 18 to 22 strokes per minute, drive 1 count, recovery 2 counts

mistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight like ropes until the legs are nearly flat.
Count 1 on the drive and 1, 2 on the recovery.

mistakes.fault: Knees bend before the handle passes them on the return
mistakes.fix: Arms and body first, then the knees, so the handle clears your knees.

cues.text: Catch: shins vertical, arms straight, lean from the hips
Then swing the body back from the hips
Arms last: elbows close to your sides, shoulders down
